svg.title: Where the French actually live — one dot per 25,000 residents
svg.desc: Dot-density map of metropolitan France. Each dot is 25,000 residents, scattered at random inside the department they live in and coloured by macro-region. Dots crowd around Paris and along the Atlantic and Mediterranean coasts; the rural diagonal from the Ardennes to the Pyrenees stays nearly empty. About 65 million residents in total.
svg.text: One dot = 25,000 residents · people ring the coasts and pack the Paris basin, leaving the rural diagonal bare

g.title: Île-de-France & North: about 23.9 million residents (957 dots)
Atlantic West: about 16.5 million residents (661 dots)
Mediterranean South: about 11.0 million residents (441 dots)
Rhône–Alps East: about 10.9 million residents (433 dots)
Central rural belt: about 2.6 million residents (102 dots)
Central rural belt: about 2.6 million residents

svg.text: Dots randomly placed within each department, not at real addresses · illustrative figures · equal-area projection
